name: Palacio de la Isla, Burgos (Franco HQ)
story: Burgos was the political capital of Nationalist Spain: the Junta de Defensa Nacional sat here from July 1936, and on 1 October 1936 Franco was invested as head of state at the city's Capitanía General. From August 1937 until October 1939 this early-20th-century mansion on the Paseo de la Isla served as his residence and headquarters. His first government was formed in Burgos in January 1938, and here on 1 April 1939 he signed the final war communiqué: 'the war has ended'. The palace now houses the Instituto Castellano y Leonés de la Lengua.
see: A neo-Renaissance mansion set in gardens on the Paseo de la Isla, west of the old town, beside the Arlanzón riverside walk.
plan: Exterior and gardens from the street; the council lists weekday visiting hours for the interior. 15 minutes' walk from the cathedral; combine with the Capitanía General building on Plaza de Alonso Martínez.
